tools.name: pixel_help
tools.description: Start here before drawing pixel art, sprites, tiles, icons, effects or animations. Returns a short quick start: the recipe format, the operations, the tools and the workflow. Pass a topic only when you need more: guide (the full authoring reference), workflow (art workflow: poses, scenes, particles, fluids, lighting), schema (the recipe JSON Schema), example (a complete recipe), or poses, scenes, autotile, fx, fluid or normals for those source formats' schemas.

tools.name: pixel_validate
tools.description: Check a pixel art recipe for mistakes before inspecting or exporting it. Validate a pixel project and return its revision id, dimensions, frame timing, animations, and clipping locations. Pass fps to check the timing against a video frame grid. Saves an immutable recipe revision; no asset export.

project.description: A version-1 Pixelbolt recipe: {"version": 1, "name", "width", "height", "palette", "symbols"?, "frames": [{"name", "duration"?, "from"?, "ops"?, "layers"?}], "animations"?}. pixel_help explains it; its topic schema is the full JSON Schema. Mistakes come back with their exact path.

revision.description: Revision id from an earlier Pixelbolt response. Send it instead of project to reuse that recipe, including after restarting with the same MCP --out directory.

fps.description: Also check timing against a video frame rate (24, 25, 29.97, 30, 60 or a fraction): frameGrid lists frame durations that are not whole video frames, positions a sequence would lengthen, shorten or never show, and whether each loop closes on the grid.

tools.name: pixel_inspect
tools.description: Look at pixel art, a sprite or an animation frame by frame to check how it looks. See a project without exporting assets. Returns one PNG contact sheet of every frame (or the chosen frames, or one animation in playback order), read left to right and top to bottom, with each cell's frame name and duration. With grid: true it also returns palette-key text grids with x/y rulers for exact pixel checks. view: tile repeats frames 3x3 for seam review. view: motion accepts a pose source or explicit compile metadata with animation, optional speed and ground; reports foot slide, ground error, pose spread and loop joins with trajectory strips. Use region to zoom in. Saves an immutable recipe revision. Use this while iterating; call pixel_render to export.

project.description: A version-1 Pixelbolt recipe: {"version": 1, "name", "width", "height", "palette", "symbols"?, "frames": [{"name", "duration"?, "from"?, "ops"?, "layers"?}], "animations"?}. pixel_help explains it; its topic schema is the full JSON Schema. Mistakes come back with their exact path.

revision.description: Revision id from an earlier Pixelbolt response. Send it instead of project to reuse that recipe, including after restarting with the same MCP --out directory.

source.description: A pixelforge-poses source, instead of project/revision; compiles it with contact and joint metadata for motion review.

metadata.description: Pose metadata returned by pixel_compile with metadata:true. Needed with a compiled project/revision for contacts and joint angles; a source supplies its own.

speed.description: Motion view: horizontal speed in pixels per second.

ground.description: Motion view: ground pixel row; overrides metadata.rig.ground.

layers.description: Isolate named layers, preserving inheritance/transforms/visibility. Omits frame ops, background and final canvas corrections, which do not belong to a named layer.

reference.description: Saved revision to compare against at the same origin. Adds a before/after image and changed-pixel report.

frames.description: Frame names to show, in this order. * (any characters) and ? (one character) in a name select every matching frame in project order, such as "flash-*". Default: every frame.

animation.description: Show one animation in playback order instead of frames.

region.description: Crop every frame to this canvas rectangle. Smaller regions are shown larger.

grid.description: Also return each frame as palette-key text rows with x/y rulers. At most 16,384 pixels in total.

scale.description: Contact sheet scale. Default: the largest that fits about 1024px.

background.description: Cell background: checker (default), transparent, a palette name or a hex color.

view.description: Onion uses pink previous/cyan next poses in playback order. Motion requires animation and reports slide, signed ground error, joint seam and pose spread, with native and enlarged trajectory/timing strips. Pass source or compile metadata to measure contacts. Tile repeats each frame 3x3.

native.description: Also return a native-size contact sheet beside the enlarged view.

diagnostics.description: Advisory duplicate, empty, isolated-pixel, palette and loop-boundary evidence, original animation timing, and per-frame counts of pixels a cleanup change would alter (corners, strays).

maxCells.description: Bound the preview with evenly spaced samples; returns omitted count and original positions. Does not alter exported animation. Evenly spaced samples can alias with a repeating pattern; use step and offset to choose positions.

step.description: Keep every step-th cell of the selection (frames or animation positions), starting at offset: step 2 shows only the A frames of an A/B strobe. Applied before maxCells.

offset.description: First position the step keeps, counting from 0. Default 0; offset 1 with step 2 shows the B frames.

tools.name: pixel_patch
tools.description: Fix or tweak pixel art (one pixel, a colour, a frame or its timing) without redrawing it. Change a recipe with targeted edits instead of resending it. Pass revision or project, plus changes applied in order: {"set": path, "value": v}, {"insert": path, "value": v}, {"remove": path}, or {"paint": "frames[blink]", "value": [{"x": 9, "y": 7, "color": "k"}]}. Paint replaces exact RGBA in canvas coordinates after all layers; transparent erases. {"cleanup": "frames[run-2]", "value": {"corners": true}} proposes fixes for doubled corners and stray pixels. Other paths look like frames[blink].layers[body].ops[2].x2, palette.k or animations.idle.frames[-]. Or pass overlay to apply a saved correction overlay. The patch is atomic and the result must validate. Returns the new revision, edit details, every frame whose pixels changed (exact pixels for small changes), timing and animation changes, and a before/after PNG with one row per frame. Saves immutable base and result revisions; render the revision to export assets.

project.description: A version-1 Pixelbolt recipe: {"version": 1, "name", "width", "height", "palette", "symbols"?, "frames": [{"name", "duration"?, "from"?, "ops"?, "layers"?}], "animations"?}. pixel_help explains it; its topic schema is the full JSON Schema. Mistakes come back with their exact path.

revision.description: Revision id from an earlier Pixelbolt response. Send it instead of project to reuse that recipe, including after restarting with the same MCP --out directory.

changes.description: Edits applied in order. Paths match error paths, such as frames[3].duration; lists also accept [name] and [-] to append.

set.description: Path to replace, or an object field to add.

insert.description: List position to insert before; [-] appends.

remove.description: Object field or list item to delete.

paint.description: Frame path, such as frames[blink]. Replaces pixels in final canvas coordinates, after all layers, preserving source operations. Use transparent to erase.

grid.description: Frame path. Value: {x,y,rows,erase?,mask?}. Dots/spaces preserve; explicit erase character clears; mask x selects and dot preserves.

move.description: Frame path. Value: {x,y,w,h,dx,dy,mask?}. Moves exact pixels including corrections; erases selected source. Destination must fit.

recolor.description: Frame path. Value: {x,y,w,h,from,to,mask?}. Replaces only matching selected colors.

cleanup.description: Frame path. Value: {corners?, strays?, x?, y?, w?, h?, mask?, colors?}. Proposes fixes as canvas corrections: corners removes doubled L-shaped steps in one-pixel lines; strays gives a pixel the colour all eight neighbours share (noise, pinholes, isolated specks). Check the report and keep deliberate corners, eyes and sparks. Inspection diagnostics count both per frame.

scope.description: Canvas edits: inherited is default. frame preserves other poses by recording compensating canvas corrections, reported in edits.protected.

value.description: JSON value for set or insert; for paint, a list of {x, y, color} pixels inside the canvas (palette names or hex colors, exact RGBA replacement).

overlay.description: Apply a saved pixelforge-overlay instead of changes. Canvas-only overlays reapply when the frames they touch are unchanged (reported as rebased).

tools.name: pixel_render
tools.description: Export pixel art as game-ready files: sprite sheet, sprites, animations, GIFs or frames for a video. Render a project into PNG sprite sheet, atlas JSON, individual PNGs, APNG animations, CSS, and Canvas player. Writes a new unique folder inside the configured export directory and saves an immutable recipe revision. Returns the folder, key files (relative), frame/animation counts, actual playback, a check of what was delivered and a bounded contact sheet. Pass expect with what the user asked for, then fix every problem the check lists before handing the files on. Large previews report sample positions and omissions; all frames still export. Optionally select an animation.

project.description: A version-1 Pixelbolt recipe: {"version": 1, "name", "width", "height", "palette", "symbols"?, "frames": [{"name", "duration"?, "from"?, "ops"?, "layers"?}], "animations"?}. pixel_help explains it; its topic schema is the full JSON Schema. Mistakes come back with their exact path.

revision.description: Revision id from an earlier Pixelbolt response. Send it instead of project to reuse that recipe, including after restarting with the same MCP --out directory.

animation.description: Preview this animation in playback order. Default: preview every frame in project order. All animations are always exported.

listFiles.description: List every exported file. Default: key files plus frame/animation counts.

scale.description: Default: 1, the frames' own size. Enlarge (4 or 8) only for posting where a small sprite would look tiny.

background.description: Palette name or opaque hex colour to blend onto. Default: 1-bit transparency.

gif.description: Also write every animation as a GIF in gifs/ for sharing ({} for defaults). Exact colours, at most 256 per frame, never quantized; notes report alpha and timing changes.

sequence.description: Also write a numbered PNG sequence for a video editor into sequence/: one PNG per video frame with alpha, plus sequence.json and a README with the ffmpeg command for a .mov. The result reports timing changes and whether a loop closes on the frame grid.

animation.description: Default: the previewed animation, or the first.

step.description: Hold each sampled frame for this many video frames; 2 animates on twos.

size.description: Canvas: 720p, 1080p, 1440p, 4k, vertical, square or WIDTHxHEIGHT. Default: the sprite at scale.

scale.description: Whole-number enlargement. Default: the largest that fits the canvas, or 1 without a size.

fit.description: contain (default): the whole sprite fits the canvas. cover: the smallest scale that covers the canvas; the overhang is cropped.

offset.description: [x, y] canvas pixels added to the aligned position.

background.description: Palette name or opaque hex colour. Default: transparent.

seconds.description: Length of the clip instead of loops.

share.description: Also return a playground link that reopens this recipe in a browser.

embedRecipe.description: Embed the recipe in the exported PNGs so they reopen in the playground.

expect.description: What the user asked for: pixel size of each frame, frames, colours, background, loop, GIF scale. The reply's check lists every file that misses it and the call that fixes it.

tools.name: pixel_compile
tools.description: Build a character animation from parts, a terrain tileset, particle effects such as sparks, embers or dust, simulated smoke, fire, explosions, steam, magic swirls, water (splashes, waterfalls, drips, bubbling potions) and thick liquids (honey, slime, mud), or a lighting normal map. Compile a pixelforge-poses source (grid, bone and mass parts; relative joints, two-bone reach, authored views, tweens, relit mirrors, contacts, and idle/walk/run/jump/attack/hurt motion templates), a pixelforge-autotile template (47-tile blob or 16-tile cardinal sets), a pixelforge-fx source (seeded particle emitters baked into frames), a pixelforge-fluid source (a deterministic fluid simulation mapped onto palette ramps; loops seamlessly) or a pixelforge-normals source (a lighting normal pass derived from a colour recipe, aligned for scene lighting and editable like any recipe) into an ordinary recipe. Saves the recipe as a revision and returns a contact sheet; pass metadata: true for pose joints, contacts, markers and motion timing, the autotile mask table, particle counts, fluid peaks and per-frame figures (pixels, box, middle, amount, pieces, speed), or the normal directions.

source.description: A pixelforge-poses, pixelforge-autotile, pixelforge-fx, pixelforge-fluid or pixelforge-normals document (see pixel_help topics). A normals source's recipe may be inline, a file under the server root or {"revision": id}.

annotations.title: Compile poses, tilesets, effects or fluids

tools.name: pixel_scene
tools.description: Compose a pixel art scene or room from sprites, tilemaps and lighting. Render a pixelforge-scene manifest (placements, tilemaps with autotile legends and neighbour rules, named cues, sequences, trajectories, attachments, ground sorting, shade placements, palette themes and optional multiplied or ramp lighting, whose lights can follow placements, flicker and flash on cues) at a time in milliseconds and return the image plus placements, the lights at that time and warnings. Assets may be inline recipes, files under the server root, or {"revision": id}. Pass export: true to write a replayable scene bundle to a new folder, and sequence: { fps, size } to write the scene as numbered PNG frames for a video editor.

sequence.description: Also write a numbered PNG sequence for a video editor into sequence/: one PNG per video frame with alpha, plus sequence.json and a README with the ffmpeg command for a .mov. The result reports timing changes and whether a loop closes on the frame grid.

size.description: Canvas: 720p, 1080p, 1440p, 4k, vertical, square or WIDTHxHEIGHT. Default: the sprite at scale.

scale.description: Whole-number enlargement. Default: the largest that fits the canvas, or 1 without a size.

fit.description: contain (default): the whole sprite fits the canvas. cover: the smallest scale that covers the canvas; the overhang is cropped.

offset.description: [x, y] canvas pixels added to the aligned position.

background.description: Palette name or opaque hex colour. Default: transparent.

seconds.description: Length of the clip instead of loops.

tools.name: pixel_import
tools.description: Turn existing pixel art or a sprite sheet PNG into an editable recipe. Import a native-resolution 8-bit RGB/RGBA PNG (optionally sliced by an unscaled atlas) as an editable recipe without changing any pixel. Pass data (base64 PNG) or path (inside the server root). Saves the recipe as a revision.

path.description: PNG file path relative to the server root.

annotations.title: Import a PNG as a recipe
